text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure is considered high (hypertension) when readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.
Blood pressure is measured using two numbers. The top number is systolic pressure (when the heart beats), and the bottom number is diastolic pressure (when the heart rests between beats).

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 1 Hypertension: 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 mm Hg or higher systolic or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic.

Hypertensive Crisis / Emergency: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic. This requires immediate medical help, especially if you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, or vision changes.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more details through the American Heart Association or check guidelines at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
